goal: In the Node http adapter (lib/adapters/http.js), match the response Content-Encoding value case-insensitively, so a compressed response whose Content-Encoding is written in non-lowercase letters (e.g. 'GZIP', 'Gzip', 'GZip') is decompressed transparently, as the lowercase forms already are.
required_behavior: When config.decompress is not false, a response with Content-Encoding 'GZIP', 'Gzip' or 'GZip' (any letter case of a supported encoding) and a gzip-compressed body resolves with the decompressed body, the same as for 'gzip'.
Case-insensitive matching covers every encoding the adapter already decompresses: gzip, x-gzip, compress, x-compress, deflate and br (br only where zlib supports Brotli).
When the adapter decompresses a body sent with a non-lowercase Content-Encoding, it removes content-encoding from the response headers, as it already does for the lowercase forms.

Existing behaviour is kept: lowercase encodings still decompress, decompress: false still returns the raw compressed body, HEAD and 204 responses are still handled without error, and unknown encodings are still passed through untouched.
constraints: Do not change package.json or package-lock.json (no new dependencies).
Do not edit built or generated output (dist/**) or the type definitions (index.d.ts, index.d.cts).
Change only the Node http adapter, lib helpers it uses, and the unit tests.

ambiguity_flags: Checkable only through a scenario (qb-checks/3). The behaviour lives in the response handler of the http adapter (lib/adapters/http.js default export), so it needs an HTTP response with a chosen Content-Encoding and a compressed body. The data adapters cannot pass a transport function, and scenarios may not use http/net. So each scenario loads ./lib/axios.js and passes config.transport: an in-process stub whose request() returns an EventEmitter request and answers with a PassThrough response (statusCode 200, lowercase header names as Node gives them, the chosen content-encoding value). This runs the adapter's real decompression path, but not a real socket. config.transport is an existing public option of the http adapter. On the base commit each scenario fails (the body stays compressed). The author also ran a control on the base with the same scenarios using lowercase spellings, and they passed; that control is not a solution. Risk: the scenario requires the ES module graph of lib/axios.js, which itself imports http, https and follow-redirects. It loaded with require on the author's local Node v20.20.2 (QB uses Node 24, not tried). If QB's runner forbids those built-ins transitively, or cannot load the graph, the checks will error and AC-1..AC-3 stay unresolved; report that rather than work around it. No check is tied to a specific helper name, since the task does not name one.

Which encodings are in scope: the issue names only gzip spellings ('Gzip', 'GZIP', 'GZip') but says 'header value should be case-insensitive'. AC-2 extends the matching to every encoding the adapter already supports; a reviewer may narrow it to gzip only.
AC-3 (header removed after decompression) is inferred from the adapter's existing lowercase behaviour, not stated in the issue.
Out of scope and unspecified: surrounding whitespace (' gzip '), and multiple or stacked encodings ('gzip, br'). The contract neither requires nor forbids handling them.
Should the Content-Encoding value in response.headers keep its original case when decompress is false or the encoding is unknown? Assumed: unchanged (left as the server sent it).
The issue's 'Browser: chrome' field is ignored: the reported adapter is http (Node), and the browser xhr adapter does not decompress itself.
